'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Eurovision Song Contest 2026]], [[Boycotts of Israel]]
**[[Iceland in the Eurovision Song Contest|Iceland]] announces that it will join [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], [[Netherlands|the Netherlands]], [[Spain|Spain]], and [[Slovenia|Slovenia]] in [[boycott]]ing next year's [[Eurovision Song Contest]] in [[Austria]] in protest of [[Israel in the Eurovision Song Contest|Israel]]'s participation. [https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/iceland-boycott-2026-eurovision-protest-go-ahead-israel-2025-12-10/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Fez buildings collapse]]
**Twenty-two people are killed and several more injured during the collapse of two adjacent buildings in [[Fez, Morocco|Fez]], [[Morocco]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-19-killed-collapse-two-buildings-moroccos-fes-state-news-agency-says-2025-12-10/ (Reuters)]
*At least one person is killed and two others are injured when a fire engulfs a large market in [[Saint Petersburg]], [[Russia]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/video-massive-fire-erupts-at-st-petersburgs-historic-soviet-era-market-1-killed-9789124 (NDTV)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Bolivia–Israel relations]]
**[[Bolivia]] and [[Israel]] formally restore [[Diplomacy|diplomatic relations]], which were severed in response to the [[Gaza war]] by former [[President of Bolivia|Bolivian president]] [[Luis Arce]] in 2023. [https://apnews.com/article/bolivia-israel-rodrigo-paz-gideon-saar-evo-morales-gaza-8482c0d13b2d3b571378ae48f33693c2 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2025 Beninese coup attempt]]
**[[Benin]]'s [[Government of Benin|government]] reports that Lieutenant Colonel [[Pascal Tigri]], identified as the leader of the failed [[Coup d'état|coup]] attempt, flees to [[Togo]], becoming the subject of an [[extradition]] request following arrests linked to the plot. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/leader-foiled-benin-coup-attempt-has-sought-refuge-togo-benin-says-2025-12-10/ (Reuters)]
*[[2025 Louvre heist]]
**The [[France|French]] [[Ministry of Culture (France)|cultural ministry]] reports to the [[Senate (France)|Senate]] that the [[Louvre]]'s [[closed-circuit television camera]] captured the October [[French Crown Jewels|jewel]] [[Art theft|theft]] but was unmonitored at the time, adding that the lapses form part of a wider inquiry into related procedural and equipment failures. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/french-watchdog-details-uncertainty-louvre-security-cameras-heist/story?id=128277660 (ABC News)]
*[[Flood control projects scandal in the Philippines]]
**[[Philippine]] [[President of the Philippines|president]] [[Bongbong Marcos]] announces the cancellation of former [[Ako Bicol]] [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|representative]] [[Zaldy Co]]'s [[Philippine passport|passport]] and directs government agencies to facilitate Co's return to the Philippines as investigators examine his alleged involvement in a large-scale [[Flood management|flood control]] [[Corruption in the Philippines|corruption]] scheme. [https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/philippines/zaldy-co-in-portugal-passport-of-fugitive-filipino-ex-congressman-cancelled-1.500375074 (''Gulf News'')]
*[[Terrorism in Canada]]
**[[Canada]] designates [[764 (organization)|764]], [[Islamic State – Mozambique Province]], [[Terrorgram]], and [[Maniac Murder Cult]] as [[List of organizations designated as terrorist by Canada|terrorist entities]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/764-youth-extremist-group-9.7010571 (CBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/canada-lists-four-extremist-insurgent-groups-foreign-terrorist-entities-2025-12-10/ (Reuters)]
*Former Bolivian president Luis Arce is arrested as part of an investigation into alleged [[embezzlement]] during his tenure as [[Ministry of Economy (Bolivia)|economy minister]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/bolivia-ex-president-arce-arrested-former-minister-says-2025-12-10/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Bulgarian budget protests]]
**Tens of thousands of people hold nationwide protests in [[Bulgaria]], calling for [[Prime Minister of Bulgaria|Prime Minister]] [[Rosen Zhelyazkov]]'s [[Zhelyazkov Government|government]] to resign over alleged [[Corruption in Bulgaria|corruption]] and dissatisfaction with proposed fiscal measures. [https://apnews.com/article/bulgaria-government-protest-corruption-a3ff3cde1b50e6b1519103dd513ac4ee (AP)]
*[[2025 Honduran general election]]
**Supporters of the ruling [[Liberty and Refoundation]] party hold protests across [[Honduras]], demanding the results of the [[President of Honduras|presidential]] election to be [[List of annulled elections|annulled]] after prolonged delays in the vote count and allegations of [[Electoral fraud|fraud]], and calling for a rerun of the election. [https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/9131812/protests-in-honduras-amid-further-election-result-delay/ (AAP via ''The Canberra Times'')]
*[[Arrest of Jair Bolsonaro]]
**The [[Brazil]]ian [[Chamber of Deputies (Brazil)|Chamber of Deputies]] approves a bill that reduces penalties for certain [[Crime in Brazil|crimes]], including attempted [[Coup d'état|coup]], which could significantly shorten former [[President of Brazil|president]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]]'s 27-year prison sentence. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20251210-ruckus-in-brazil-congress-over-bid-to-reduce-bolsonaro-jail-term (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Censorship in Vietnam]]
**The [[Vietnam]]ese [[National Assembly of Vietnam|National Assembly]] adopts amendments to [[Television and mass media in Vietnam|its press]] and [[Classified information|state secrets]] laws that expand [[Government of Vietnam|government]] authority to compel journalists to disclose sources and broaden the range of information classified as state secrets. [https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/vietnam-set-make-it-harder-media-protect-sources-expand-state-secrets-2025-12-10/ (Reuters)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Brazil–China relations]]
**[[Science and technology in Brazil|Brazil]] and [[Science and technology in China|China]] begin constructing a joint laboratory for [[Radio astronomy|radio astronomic]] technology with the [[Federal University of Campina Grande]] and the [[Federal University of Paraíba]] to support [[space research]] as both countries work on the [[BINGO (telescope)|BINGO]] [[radio telescope]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/china-brazil-create-joint-space-laboratory-despite-us-pressure-2025-12-10/ (Reuters)]
